Messages.Author: firstco...@aol.com
Messages.Body:
Questions about "Punish",
not "LSJ should punish questions" :)

First, some setup using precedents:

I strike with Theft of Vitae, you strike with Undead Strength. Both
resolve during strike resolution, meaning I gain 2 from you, and am
assigned 3 damage. After excess blood has drained off, there's a
chance to prevent damage.

If I strike with Entombment and you strike with Undead Strength, then
you go to torpor at the same time that my Undead Strength hits you for
3, before damage is resolved. When strikes resolve, you're in torpor,
so combat ends--but I still have 3 damage to take and can play Skin of
Rock (even though combat's ended.)

(Is this correct?)

I strike with Blood Fury, which reads in part that if you strike with a
weapon this round, you do no damage. You strike with a weapon. Both
take effect immediately. Damage from your weapon is what, not
assigned? Or assigned, and then reduced to 0?

Finally, Punish's relevant text:
[ACTION] +1 stealth action. (D) Put this card on a vampire. You still
control this card. The vampire with this card cannot gain blood. Any
blood he or she gains goes to the blood bank instead. Burn this card
during your next untap phase.
[COMBAT] As [ACTION] above, but put this card on the opposing vampire
as a hand strike (at strength damage) instead.

I strike with Punish. You strike with Theft of Vitae.

A) Both resolve simultaneously. Like with Entombment and Undead
Strength, both effects are applied, and carried out, and any sort of
"preventative measure" will not stop the other thing (cause it's not in
effect until it resolves, at which point the other has resolved also).
B) Both resolve simultaneously. Like with Blood Fury, the blood you
gain is negated by this card's effect.
C) Something else. There's an "order of resolution", or some such.

That's all. Trying to understand strike resolution as "simultaneous",
and apply it to the game.

-- Brian

Well, you don't go to torpor until after strike resolution is finished
(you're just "wounded" -- bound for torpor -- until then).

> I strike with Blood Fury, which reads in part that if you strike with a
> weapon this round, you do no damage. You strike with a weapon. Both
> take effect immediately. Damage from your weapon is what, not
> assigned? Or assigned, and then reduced to 0?

Shouldn't matter, but if it does, "reduced to zero, then assigned".
Blood Fury being the exception to the rule, since it affects
simultaneously-resolving strikes.

> Finally, Punish's relevant text:
> [ACTION] +1 stealth action. (D) Put this card on a vampire. You still
> control this card. The vampire with this card cannot gain blood. Any
> blood he or she gains goes to the blood bank instead. Burn this card
> during your next untap phase.
> [COMBAT] As [ACTION] above, but put this card on the opposing vampire

> I strike with Punish. You strike with Theft of Vitae.
>
> A) Both resolve simultaneously. Like with Entombment and Undead
> Strength, both effects are applied, and carried out, and any sort of

> effect until it resolves, at which point the other has resolved also).

A.
